extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, EPO practitioners, and IP counsel (particularly those working on AI-related inventions)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of substantive updates in the EPO Guidelines for Examination 2024, focusing on entitlement to priority, inventive-step evidence standards, opposition acceleration with UPC cases, and disclosure requirements for AI-related patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to priority (A-III, 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated EPO Guidelines concern the entitlement to priority (A-III, 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for inventive step (G-VII, 5.2, 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates to the evidence standard for inventive step reflecting recent decisions of the EPO’s Enlarged Board of Appeal on G 1/22 and G 2/21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines have been amended to reflect the Enlarged Board decisions (G 1/22 and G 2/21) on how evidence for inventive step should be assessed; the page notes these specific guideline sections (G-VII, 5.2, 11) but does not restate the full evidentiary tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration of opposition proceedings where UPC actions are pending (D-VII, 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceleration of opposition proceedings in cases of pending actions before the Unified Patent Court (D-VII, 1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines include provisions to expedite opposition proceedings when there are pending UPC actions; reference given to section D-VII, 1.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirements for AI inventions — general
rubrics_metrics.description: EPC Guidelines update disclosure requirements for AI inventions (F-III, 3), underlining the importance for patent applications claiming inventions relating to AI to disclose the mathematical methods and the training datasets to the extent needed to reproduce the technical effect over the whole range claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines state that applicants should disclose mathematical methods and training datasets to the extent necessary to reproduce the claimed technical effect across the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-of-technical-effect standard for AI inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When it comes to proof of technical effects: "while mere allegations are not enough, comprehensive proof is not required either."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a middle evidentiary standard: applicants must provide more than allegations but are not required to furnish exhaustive proof of technical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of training dataset characteristics when effect depends on them
rubrics_metrics.description: If the technical effect is dependent on particular characteristics of the training dataset used, those characteristics that are required to reproduce the technical effect must be disclosed unless the skilled person can determine them without undue burden using common general knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose dataset characteristics necessary to reproduce the technical effect over the whole range claimed, except where such characteristics can be derived by the skilled person from common general knowledge without undue burden.
